records.issue_text: checkIfIsAvailable skips the busy/booking check entirely when a slot falls inside a date override, allowing double-booking because it returns early when dateOverrideExist is true
records.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, after the date-override scan, the function returns early when a date override exists for that day: `if (dateOverrideExist) { return true; }`. This occurs *before* the final `return busy.every((busyTime) => { ... })` busy/conflict check, so any slot that falls on a day with a date override will be marked available without considering `busy` (and thus can allow double-booking except for the earlier `currentSeats` exact-start-time guard).

records.rationale: In `checkIfIsAvailable`, the slot date is explicitly taken in UTC (`const slotStartTime = time.utc();`), and the date-override match compares that UTC date string against a shifted organizer-local override date: `dayjs(date.start).add(utcOffset, "minutes").format(...) === slotStartTime.format(...)`. This mixes organizer-local (override) logic with a UTC day boundary (slot), so around midnight for non-zero offsets, overrides and slots can fall on different calendar days and be misclassified.

records.issue_text: Unreliable parsing via Date.prototype.toString() (non-ISO, engine-dependent format) passed to dayjs can yield Invalid Date/NaN offsets poisoning startTime/endTime; should use toISOString() or pass the Date directly
records.rationale: In `packages/lib/slots.ts`, the new logic computes offsets using `dayjs(override.start.toString()).tz(override.timeZone).utcOffset()` and similarly for `timeZone`. Passing `Date.prototype.toString()` (non-ISO, locale/engine-dependent) forces Dayjs to re-parse a string; if parsing fails it can produce an invalid date and `utcOffset()` may become `NaN`, which then propagates into `add(offset, "minute")` when computing `startTime`/`endTime`. The diff shows this exact pattern and it is avoidable by passing the `Date` directly or using `toISOString()`.

records.issue_text: Round-robin path can yield organizerTimeZone: undefined, silently falling back to utcOffset = 0 and producing wrong availability instead of an explicit failure
records.rationale: In the round-robin branch, `organizerTimeZone` is passed as `userSchedule?.timeZone` (see `const userSchedule = userAvailability.find(...); ... organizerTimeZone: userSchedule?.timeZone`). If `find` returns `undefined` (or `timeZone` is unset), `checkIfIsAvailable` receives `organizerTimeZone: undefined` and explicitly falls back to `utcOffset = 0` (`organizerTimeZone ? ... : 0`), which can silently compute availability using the wrong offset rather than failing or handling the missing timezone.
